title: Adic formal smoothness gives lifts into complete rings along closed ideals
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal such that $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $A$ be a commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $J^t\subseteq I$ for some $t\ge1$ and $J=\bigcap_{m\ge1}(J+I^m)$ ($J$ is closed for the $I$-adic topology). Let $q:A\to A/J$ be the quotient map, with $A/J$ an $R$-algebra via $q$, and let $g:S\to A/J$ be a homomorphism of $R$-algebras such that $g(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq q(I)$ for some $r\ge1$. Then there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to A$ with $q\circ f=g$, and $f(\mathfrak n^{rt})\subseteq I$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, line 9257) and its proof, for $R$ with the discrete topology (Definition Tag 07NI, definition-formally-smooth-adic, line 9213, condition (2)(b)); 'A adic' is Definition Tag 07E8 (definition-topological-ring, line 8959) (8): pre-adic with ideal of definition I and complete, i.e. A -> lim A/I^n bijective; continuity of g for the I-adic quotient topology on A/J is, by Lemma Tag 07E9 (lemma-continuous), g(n^r) in (I+J)/J for some r

proof.text: *The finite quotients and the first row.* For integers $a,b\geq1$ put $A_{a,b}=A/(J^a+I^b)$, with its $R$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The quotient maps in either index make the $A_{a,b}$ a commutative grid of discrete $R$-algebras. Since $J$ is closed, the canonical map $A/J\to\varprojlim_b A/(J+I^b)=\varprojlim_bA_{1,b}$ is bijective. Its kernel is $\bigcap_b(J+I^b)/J=0$. For surjectivity, choose representatives $x_b\in A$ of a compatible family, successively adjusting $x_{b+1}$ by an element of $J$ so that $x_{b+1}-x_b\in I^b$; the adjusted representatives give a compatible family in $A/I^b$, hence an element $x\in A$ by $I$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and its class modulo $J+I^b$ is the prescribed one. Define $\varphi_{1,b}:S\to A_{1,b}$ as $g$ followed by $A/J\to A_{1,b}$. These maps are compatible in $b$. Moreover $g(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq q(I)$ implies $\varphi_{1,1}(\mathfrak n^r)=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, lines 9274-9289): $A_{n,m}$, $A/J=\varprojlim A/(J+I^m)$, and the maps $\varphi_{1,m}$

proof.text: *The square-zero maps in the grid.* For $a,b\geq1$ there is a natural surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras $$A_{a+1,b+1}\longrightarrow A_{a+1,b}\times_{A_{a,b}}A_{a,b+1}.$$ Indeed, for ideals $K=J^{a+1}+I^b$ and $L=J^a+I^{b+1}$, the usual map $A\to A/K\times_{A/(K+L)}A/L$ is onto: if representatives $x,y$ have the same image modulo $K+L$, write $x-y=k+\ell$ with $k\in K$, $\ell\in L$, and the class of $x-k=y+\ell$ gives a preimage. Here $K+L=J^a+I^b$, and $D=J^{a+1}+I^{b+1}\subseteq K\cap L$, so the map factors through $A/D=A_{a+1,b+1}$. Its kernel is $(K\cap L)/D$. In $A/D$, the image of $K=J^{a+1}+I^b$ is contained in the image of $I^b$; hence the square of the kernel is contained in the image of $I^{2b}$, which is zero because $2b\geq b+1$ and $I^{b+1}\subseteq D$. Thus the kernel has square zero.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, lines 9281-9293): the displayed grid and the square-zero surjection; the ideal calculation is written out here

proof.text: *Construction of compatible maps on the grid.* Starting with $\varphi_{1,1}$, lift successively along $A_{a+1,1}\to A_{a,1}$ to obtain compatible $R$-algebra maps $\varphi_{a,1}:S\to A_{a,1}$. The kernel of this transition has square zero because $(J^a+I)^2\subseteq J^{a+1}+I$ for $a\geq1$. The initial map kills $\mathfrak n^r$, and after every square-zero lift the lifted map kills the square of any power killed by its reduction (remark (a) in [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]); hence every map to be lifted kills some power of $\mathfrak n$. Thus the lifting property in [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] applies at every finite stage. Induct on $a+b$ for the remaining entries. If $\varphi_{a+1,b}$ and $\varphi_{a,b+1}$ have been constructed compatibly, their pair is a map from $S$ to $A_{a+1,b}\times_{A_{a,b}}A_{a,b+1}$ which kills some power of $\mathfrak n$ (take the larger of the two exponents). Lift it through the square-zero surjection of step 2 to $\varphi_{a+1,b+1}$. Induction gives maps $\varphi_{a,b}$ compatible with every horizontal and vertical transition.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, lines 9294-9308): induction along the bottom row and then on $n+m$

proof.text: *The compatible diagonal and the limit map.* Since $J^t\subseteq I$, one has $J^{bt}\subseteq I^b$ for every $b\geq1$, so $A_{bt,b}=A/(J^{bt}+I^b)=A/I^b$. Let $f_b:S\to A/I^b$ be $\varphi_{bt,b}$ under this equality. Grid compatibility shows that the reduction of $f_{b+1}$ modulo $I^b$ is $f_b$: reduce $\varphi_{(b+1)t,b+1}$ first in the two indices to $\varphi_{bt,b}$. Therefore the $f_b$ define an $R$-algebra homomorphism $f:S\to\varprojlim_bA/I^b=A$, where the last equality is the given $I$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, lines 9309-9312): $\varphi_b=\varphi_{bt,b}$ and passage to $A=\varprojlim A/I^b$

proof.text: *Agreement modulo $J$.* For each $b$, compatibility of the grid identifies the composite $S\xrightarrow{f}A\to A/(J+I^b)$ with $\varphi_{1,b}$, which by step 1 is the reduction of $g$. Hence the two maps $q\circ f,g:S\to A/J$ have the same composite to every $A/(J+I^b)$. The injectivity of $A/J\to\varprojlim_bA/(J+I^b)$ from step 1 gives $q\circ f=g$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous, lines 9311-9314): agreement with $\psi$ through $A/J=\varprojlim A/(J+I^b)$

proof.text: *The asserted adic bound.* Since $qf=g$ and $g(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq q(I)=(I+J)/J$, one has $f(\mathfrak n^r)\subseteq I+J$. Therefore $$f(\mathfrak n^{rt})\subseteq(I+J)^t\subseteq I+J^t\subseteq I.$$ For the middle inclusion, every product of $t$ factors from $I+J$ either has a factor in $I$ and hence lies in $I$, or has all factors in $J$ and hence lies in $J^t$. This proves both the required lift and the final inclusion.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks More on Algebra 07NJ and kept unchanged. The proof follows 07NJ in six steps: define the finite quotient grid and identify A/J with its inverse limit using closedness of J and I-adic completeness; prove the grid maps are surjective with square-zero kernel; construct compatible lifts first along the bottom row and then by induction on the two indices, explicitly checking that each map kills a power of n so the stated adic formal-smoothness definition applies; take the diagonal (bt,b) and the inverse limit; check agreement modulo J; prove f(n^{rt}) is contained in I. No new nodes: the only inputs are the three existing statement dependencies, and all omitted source calculations are elementary ideal and inverse-limit calculations written in the steps. Existing Mathlib searches already include LeanSearch, LeanFinder/Loogle, local search and grep and show only the discrete-formal-smoothness special case.
